resources.string: Keep your Mac and phone on the same local network. Choose the Mac, compare the pairing code, then confirm it on both devices. Optional permissions are requested only when you enable the related feature.
Your paired Mac can browse and download files from the folders you add here. Bridgey cannot see anything else on this phone.
Allow the Mac to add files
Files from the Mac get a new name when one is taken. Nothing is replaced.
Clipboard, files, Ping and Ring go to the selected device.
Waiting for the Mac to share its actions.
Nothing is allowed yet. Choose actions in Bridgey Settings on the Mac.
The Mac no longer allows this. Check Mac actions in Bridgey Settings on the Mac.
The Mac could not read the request
Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.
A Shortcut is still running on the Mac
The Mac needs Accessibility access first. Open Bridgey on the Mac.
Not available on the Mac right now: the app is gone or there is no sound output

Lock, sleep and volume for your paired Mac
Pair a Mac in Bridgey first
Allow Lock, Sleep or Volume in Bridgey Settings on the Mac
Device controls and the Bridgey home-screen widget offer the Mac actions your Mac allows.
Send this link from %1$s to your Mac?
The Mac shows it until you open or dismiss it there.
Battery optimization is off for Bridgey
Battery optimization is on for Bridgey, so Android may pause the connection in the background
a private network (VPN or carrier NAT)

Allow notifications to share your screen?
While your screen is shared, Bridgey keeps a notification with Stop visible. Allow Bridgey notifications first, then tap Share again.
Shown for as long as a Mac sees this screen
Your screen is being shared with %1$s
Tap Stop to end it. Turning off the screen ends it too.
Waiting for the Mac to open its window…

Optional permissions: Notifications keep the connection, file transfers and Find Device visible. Notification access forwards notifications to your Mac. Phone lets your Mac start, answer and end calls. Each is requested only when you turn on that feature. Review them any time in Settings, Permissions.
Bridgey asks for a permission only when you turn on the feature that needs it. Denying a permission turns off only that feature.
Keep the connection, file transfers, received files and Find Device visible.
Reads notification titles and text and sends them only to your paired Mac.
Lets your paired Mac start calls and answer, decline or end them. Bridgey does not read contacts or call history.
Finding and connecting to your Mac on the local network needs no permission. Bridgey never asks for location, contacts, SMS, camera or microphone access.
Deletes paired devices, settings and the recent transfer list on this phone.
Deleted: paired Macs and their keys, all settings and per-device choices, the notification application list, call settings and the recent transfer list. The welcome guide shows again.
Kept: received files in Download/Bridgey, permissions granted in Android Settings, and this phone’s identity. Your Macs keep their record of this phone until you forget it there.
